alternative_explanations: The advance estimate will be revised as source data are completed.
Imports subtract from the GDP accounting identity and do not on their own signify weaker domestic demand.
analysis.behavioral_readout: The combination is more consistent with private domestic spending remaining firmer than the GDP headline than with a broad domestic-demand collapse, because final sales to private domestic purchasers accelerated even as government spending, investment and exports reduced headline momentum.
caveats: Quarterly growth is annualised and not directly comparable to month-on-month or year-on-year rates.
changes: Headline real GDP slowed from 2.1% SAAR in Q1 to 1.5% in Q2.
Consumer spending, investment and exports increased, while government spending decreased; imports also increased.
The domestic-purchases price index accelerated to 5.7% from 3.6%.
analysis.headline: US real GDP grew at a 1.5% annualised rate in Q2, slower than Q1, while private domestic final sales accelerated to 3.9%.
implications: Inference: the softer headline does not by itself show a comparable weakening of private domestic demand.
verification_needed: BEA GDP second estimate for Q2 on 26 August 2026.
BEA component revisions for consumption, investment and government spending.

values.metric: Real final sales to private domestic purchasers
